subject: AvatarX-v2: elevated 5xx/timeouts — recovery update, mitigation and closure plan
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, ops@avatarx.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: AvatarX-v2: elevated 5xx/timeouts observed (initial alert)

Morning team / Claire,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and timeout errors for the AvatarX-v2 model at ~07:52 PDT. Error rate peaked around 12% of requests for ~30 minutes, primarily 503/504 and tokenization timeouts on longer context requests (16k+).

What we've captured so far:
- Window: 07:52–08:30 PDT, spike mostly on region-us-east.
- Errors: 503 gateway, 504 generation timeouts, and occasional model runtime OOMs on 16k seq workloads.
- Client impact: AvatarX reporting elevated failed calls for their batch inference and streaming endpoints.

I've attached a short snippet of service logs and example traces. Can ops confirm if any kernel rollouts, quantization toggles, or autoscale pushes were active from 07:30–08:00?

Claire — apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as an active incident; will follow up with an ops summary and a customer-facing note in the next 30–45 minutes.

Attachments: avatarx_error_snippet.log (text)

Best,
Ava
Ava Chen
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@avatarx.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AvatarX-v2: elevated 5xx/timeouts observed (ops triage)

On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 8:12 AM Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Morning team / Claire,
> ...

Thanks Ava — quick ops notes: we've rolled the serving fleet to an older kernel variant (kernel-v2-stable) for AvatarX-v2 at 08:18 PDT which immediately reduced the 503 surface, and we enabled the lightweight fallback model (avatarx-v2-rtx-quant) for requests flagged as long-context.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Kernel rollback to kernel-v2-stable (08:18).
- Enabled fallback variant for sequences >12k.
- Temporarily increased the autoscale floor for the tenant pool by +20% (no billing changes until we validate).

Next steps (short):
- Collect complete trace set and KV-cache eviction stats (INF-4521).
- Run targeted canary on avatarx batch jobs for 2 hours.
- Draft customer-facing update (Ava to send).

I'll own the runbook follow-up and Jira.

Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: ops@avatarx.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: AvatarX-v2 — customer update: mitigation in place and next steps

Claire / Sean,

Summary update: we performed an emergency rollback to kernel-v2-stable and enabled the long-context fallback variant at ~08:18 PDT. After those actions we observed error rates fall from ~12% to ~1.2% within ~10 minutes, and from 08:40–09:00 the traffic profile looks stable.

Why this happened (short, interim):
- Trigger: a recent kernel optimization (kernel-v2-experimental) interacts poorly with our KV-cache eviction threshold for sequences >12k when batching variability is high — that led to increased cache misses, heavier recomputation, and transient resource contention.
- Impact: higher latencies causing upstream gateway retries and generation timeouts for longer context requests.

What we did:
- Rolled back kernel to kernel-v2-stable (08:18 PDT).
- Enabled avatarx-v2-rtx-quant fallback for >12k contexts.
- Increased tenant pool floor by +20% while we confirm stability.

What we will do next (action items):
1) Rishi/ops to collect full traces and KV-cache metrics (INF-4521) — ETA 4 hours.
2) Engineering to verify root cause in staging and produce a targeted patch for kernel selection logic — ETA 72 hours for hotfix; deeper scheduling fix by 3 weeks.
3) We will produce a short postmortem and remediation plan; link to the draft will be shared within 24 hours.

Temporary customer accommodations:
- We'll apply a one-time incident credit on your September usage invoice for the impacted window (details to follow).

Please let us know if you need any immediate manual retries for queued batch jobs — we can coordinate a controlled re-run once you confirm the list.

Attachments: avatarx_rca_draft.pdf (interim technical note)

Thanks again for the patience — we'll follow up with trace data and the postmortem link shortly.

Ava
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: ops@avatarx.com, ava@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: AvatarX-v2 — final postmortem and remediation commitments

Claire / Sean / team,

Follow-up with the finalized postmortem attached. Key items:
- Root cause: kernel-v2-experimental kernel selection + KV-cache eviction regression under high-batch-variability for seq >12k.
- Short-term fixes completed: kernel rollback, fallback enabled, autoscale floor increased, targeted canary.
- Long-term remediation: improve kernel selection unit tests, add a KV-cache monotonicity check to the runtime (INF-4521), and add an automated health-check for long-context batches.

Timeline and commitments:
- Hotpatch (kernel-selection guard): scheduled 2026-10-01 02:00–04:00 UTC (ETA: 72 hours from initial incident).
- Full scheduling fix and additional regression tests: targeted completion by 2026-10-20.
- Postmortem doc & remediation list: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-avatarx-postmortem

We've applied the customer credit for the impacted window; accounting will send a separate invoice note. If you'd like a joint postmortem review call, we can schedule one this week — propose Thu 10/1 09:00 PDT.

Attachments: postmortem_avatarx.docx (docx)

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
